summary:
# NOTES ON THE THREE BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 — "Jimmy Quixote: A Novel" by Tom Gallon (Hurst and Blackett, 1906)
Dedication to Malcolm Watson. Chapters: I "Old Paul's Babies"; II "And Old Paul's Friends"; III "Jimmy Quixote"; IV "The Eloping Persons"; V "Jimmy's Affections"; VI "Mrs. Baffall's Dream"; VII "Over the Hills and Far Away". Book II: I "The Call of the World"; II "Jimmy—and a Matter of Food"; III "The Complete Letter-Writer"; IV "The Man in Print"; V "Another Taste of Bohemia"; VI "Charlie Plunges"; VII "Dreams"; VIII "The Sides of the 'Buses O!"; IX "The Dawn". Book III: I "'It'll Be All Right'"; II "Jimmy Quixote"; III "Two Ways of Love"; IV "The Long Night"; V "'If I Might Die!'"; VI "The Spirit of Old Paul".

**Characters:** Old Paul = Paul Nannock (tall, shy, blushing, Daisley Cross, house "Daisley Place"; died on stairs after writing will "To Moira, beloved of my heart now and always"); Patience (Roe), old servant, sharp-tongued, loves Paul; Anthony Ditchburn (self-styled scholar, tobacco-loving, sponger, quotes Horace; later begs and dies bitter); Moira (dark-eyed, mother was Paul's lost love; Paul's "little maid"); Jimmy Larrance (Jimmy Quixote, boy hero, later writer, fights bullies, marries Moira out of promise to dying Charlie; later loves Alice, then reconciles with Moira; child named Moira); Alice Vickery (fair, pretty, flirtatious, later marries Ashby Feak? — she is with Jimmy then "engaged"; ultimately she is the "butterfly"); Rev. Temple Purdue (mild rector); Charlie Purdue (rector's son, kisses Moira, fights Jimmy, later plunges into debt, seduces Moira, dies after accident, sends for Jimmy: "It'll be all right"); Mr. Daniel Baffall & Mrs. Flora Baffall (retired London tradespeople, childless, kind); Honora Jackman (loud, eyeglass, flirts with Jimmy, kisses him; sings; leaves); Eli? (no, not in this book); Lucas Savell? (not here). Others: Mr. Matthew Shandler (second cousin, claims estate); Felix? no. Gavin? no. Moggs no. Mrs. Hoffman no. Ashby Feak no. Ponder: Book 1 characters are Hurst.

**Plot events:** Paul brings home parcels, shawl for Patience, cricket bat/rod for Jimmy, dolls for girls. Paul's past: loved a woman, she left him for richer man, died; her child Moira left to him. Jimmy orphan, Alice's mother flung her at Paul. Anthony Ditchburn arrives in storm; tutors fail; Rector Purdue teaches children; Charlie Purdue joins. Baffalls adopt Alice-figure. Honora Jackman seduces Jimmy into revealing the hidden glade; Paul catches her; "Jimmy Quixote" name given. Elopement with donkey "the Ancient One" and chaise. Honora's farewell; Jimmy's letter. Charlie kisses Moira in race; Jimmy fights Charlie in wood (Jimmy: "Say you're sorry"). Paul goes to London, learns he is dying; night talk with Mrs. Baffall at her window; dies on stairs. Matthew Shandler takes estate; house sold; Patience and Moira go to London (Chelsea); Jimmy to London warehouse (Baffall recommendation). Moira writes to Alice; Patience writes black-edged letter claiming wealth; Baffalls/Purdue plot to send Charlie to Patience's rooms. Charlie visits Moira, takes her to opera (Faust) and Bohemia music hall; Charlie moves downstairs; seduces Moira after she's upset. Jimmy becomes writer: "Idea", editors, Bennett Godsby stage play; Alice attends. Moira comes to Jimmy's rooms, says she will marry Charlie. Charlie in debt; father's £50; Charlie's fall in Moira's room (night, Moira goes out to theatre, comes back, Charlie seduces her in grief). Moira pregnant; Charlie dies after being struck by horses; with dying breath asks Jimmy to marry Moira, "It'll be all right." Jimmy marries Moira (cold wedding). Jimmy's affair with Alice; Ashby Feak rival. Anthony Ditchburn steals Moira's letters to Jimmy (letters show her love), Jimmy reads them; Moira leaves; Jimmy, drunk, nearly strangles her earlier (Anthony's report). Patience brings news of baby; Jimmy takes baby Moira. Reconciled at Daisley Cross graves; Moira's eyes. END BOOK 1 / BOOK 2 / BOOK 3 as tabled above.

## BOOK 2 (in the transcript) — "The Runaways" by Nat Gould (Royal Ascot Library; G. Heath Robinson & J. Birch)
Chapters: I As the Snow Falls; II The Runaways; III Random; IV Irene's Painting; V Honeysuckle's Foal; VI A Wily Young Man; VII Selling His Heritage; VIII Warren's Return; IX How Ulick Bought the Saint; X "The Curiosity"; XI For a Woman's Sake; XII Two Schemers; XIII The Squire and the Saint; XIV A Discovery Imminent; XV The Result of the Discovery; XVI A Race to Be Remembered; XVII The Squire Overhears; XVIII "Tally-ho!"; XIX A Fatal Leap; XX Perfect Harmony.

**Characters:** Redmond Maynard (Squire, Hazelwell; loyal to honour; dog Bersak wolfhound); Ulick Maynard (son, left home 2 years ago after accusation of wronging Janet Todd; bay horse Random; later owns grey colt "the Saint" bought under name Mr. Lanark); Irene Courtly (née Carstone, Colonel Carstone's daughter, ward of Squire, paints; married Warren; loves Ulick); Warren Courtly (husband, gambler, lives Anselm Manor; secretly took Janet away; dies in steeplechase-leap over churchyard wall at Glen church); Eli Todd (stud manager, Janet's father, faithful to Ulick); Janet Todd (ran off with Warren; kept at Feltham by Mrs. Hoffman as "Mrs. Warren"); Felix Hoffman (blackmailer, bookmaker's tout); Mrs. Hoffman; Honeysuckle (old mare; colt foal born 12:15 after midnight New Year's); Bob Heather (groom); Mary Marley (Irene's maid, later marries Bob); Mrs. Dixon/Martha Dixon (Anselm housekeeper); Dr. Harding; James Bard (vet, Helton); Fred May (trainer, Newmarket, Stanton House); Ben Sprig (jockey, rides the Saint; "Ben"); Kit Cat, Pinkerton, Vulture, Sandstone, Coralie, Avenger, Decoy Duck, Mermaid (horses).

**Events:** Anniversary night Redmond sits up; Irene stays. Eli's daughter Janet left same night Ulick did. Ulick visits Eli at foaling, leaves address; Warren is revealed as seducer when Ulick sees him at Mrs. Hoffman's. Ulick buys Saint for 200 guineas via Fred May. Saint wins Pastures Handicap at Kempton (Ben Sprig). Squire reconciled with Ulick at Newmarket (Eli & Fred's plot). Walton Hotel dinner. Warren sells Holme Farm for £10,000 to pay gambling debts; Felix blackmails Warren (£50); Irene gets Felix's letter, sends £5, visits Janet at Feltham, learns truth; Janet's account. Derby: Sandstone wins. Coronation Cup: Saint beats Vulture by short head. Felix insults Warren in paddock; Warren strikes him. Warren confesses to Irene; she refuses to hide it, says she loves Ulick (overheard? Squire overhears in ch XVII). Honeysuckle foal; Ulick and Random at Helton hunt; Warren challenges Ulick to follow him over Glen church wall; grey horse falls, Warren's neck broken on Harewood's vault. Warren buried at Anselm church. Janet returns to Eli, confirms Warren. Ulick and Irene marry the following summer; son born; Squire grandfather; Janet becomes Irene's maid; Felix flees country; Saint at stud. Last line: "THE END."

---

## BOOK 3 — "Tinman" by Tom Gallon (Small, Maynard & Co., Boston 1907)
Parts: PART I (ch I What I Found in the Wood; II And What I Lost; III Her Wedding Day; IV The Killing of the Lie; V Alas! for Poor Prince Charlie!; VI I Leave the World). PART II (I Mine Enemy; II Ghosts; III I Enter upon Servitude; IV The Coming of the Wolves; V I Touch Disaster; VI Love with the Veiled Face; VII News of the Prisoner; VIII I Assist the Enemy; IX I Know the Way at Last; X Too Late!; XI I Tell the Truth; XII The Haunted Man; XIII I Face the World Again).

**Narrator:** Charles Avaline, a.k.a. Tinman, later "No. 145". Guardian Jervis Fanshawe (thin, white nervous fingers twining, manager of Patton & Co., embezzler, in debt to Gavin Hockley). Gavin Hockley (big, swaggering, brutal; blackmailer). Barbara Patton (daughter of Mr. Patton of Hammerstone Market; marries Lucas Savell, cousin, good-humoured; later "Barbara Savell"; mother of Barbara II). Mr. Patton (old, dies). Lucas Savell (weak; drinks; stroke; mute). Murray Olivant (rich, cruel; half-brother of Arnold Millard; schemes against Barbara II; fakes sailing on the *Eaglet*). Arnold Millard (boy-painter, brother of Olivant, loves Barbara II). Dawkins (smiling, grins, blackmailer). Moggs (grubby street girl, helper). The stewardess (unnamed). Elder Barbara (dies "at sea" falsely; actually escaped with stewardess; lives as "Barbara Avaline"; reunites with Charlie).

**Events:** Charlie arrives London; Fanshawe's dinner with Hockley; Hammerstone Market, meets Barbara in wood; Hockley trips him; Barbara's engagement to Lucas Savell announced at dinner; Charlie strikes Hockley on terrace; card game, Charlie loses money, IOU ~£30 then £70; supper quarrel; Charlie threatens Hockley; Charlie kills Hockley in his Lincoln's Inn Fields rooms with sword; Fanshawe framed Charlie; trial, guilty, death sentence commuted to life penal servitude; Barbara visits cell (dream); Charlie 20 years in prison (No. 145, tinsmith); released; Fanshawe meets him; named "Tinman"; Olivant hires him; Barbara II; Olivant's plot; Charlie hears Barbara's dead-at-sea story; Olivant's assault on Barbara II at dinner; Charlie tied up with towel and gagged; Dawkins steals letter; Barbara II taken; Charlie frees himself; Barbara (elder) at terrace; Olivant lies; Moggs finds Barbara II; Charlie threatens Olivant; Olivant found dead, stabbed with knife in Lincoln's Inn Fields; Fanshawe did it; Fanshawe sails on Eaglet, lost in wreck off Ushant; Charlie marries elder Barbara; the Eaglet tickets; end: Barbara II married Arnold Millard; Lucas Savell stricken; Charlie and Barbara wed. Final line: "THE END."
